questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make your own face mask at home
Why face masks have always been popular in Asia
The history of the plague in Europe and its masks
Whether wearing masks in public helps stop the virus
questions.why: Rob says they'll ask whether wearing masks in public can help prevent the spread of coronavirus.

questions.q: What did Professor Robert West do?
options: He designed a new type of mask for hospitals
He reviewed over twenty studies on the evidence
He ran a big survey of people who wear masks
He tested lots of different masks in a laboratory
questions.why: Sam says he conducted a review of over twenty studies looking into the evidence.

questions.q: What does Professor West say about the evidence on masks?
options: It is unclear and doesn't tell us anything yet
It clearly shows that masks work very well
It clearly shows that masks are harmful to wear
It has not been studied by scientists at all
questions.why: He says the evidence is equivocal and doesn't tell you anything yet.

questions.q: According to Professor West, why is there such a heated debate?
options: Masks are far too expensive for many families
Governments keep changing the rules every week
People rely on opinions because the evidence is weak
Scientists refuse to share their research with others
questions.why: He says people are really relying on their opinion, which leads to heated debate.

questions.q: What is the 'stands to reason' argument for masks?
options: Doctors have always worn them during operations
Masks are now required by law in most countries
Masks make people feel calmer when they go out
A covering over your mouth traps virus droplets
questions.why: He explains that if you speak or cough into a covering, it will trap a lot of the virus droplets.

questions.q: How did the WHO advice change in June?
options: Wear masks in public where distancing isn't possible
Only carers and nurses should wear masks at work
Nobody needs to wear a mask any more, even indoors
Masks should be worn at home when family visit
questions.why: Rob says the WHO now says masks should be worn in public where social distancing isn't possible.

questions.q: What does Professor West mean by 'mask shaming'?
options: Feeling embarrassed about how your mask looks
Wearing masks because others would judge you
Companies selling poor-quality masks for high prices
Doctors refusing to wear masks in public places
questions.why: He says people feel compelled to wear masks because it's expected and they'd be judged if they didn't.

questions.q: What other problem with masks does Professor West mention?
options: They make it hard to breathe
They are bad for the environment
They can make people feel safer than they are
They stop people talking to each other
questions.why: He says masks can potentially create a false sense of security.
